summary.headline: Studds Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.7% to INR169.7 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% on a styrene-driven raw material spike; management guides 14-15% in Q2.
summary.overview:
Consolidated revenue grew 13.7% YoY to INR169.7 crores, with two-wheeler helmet and box volume of 1.95 million units at 81% utilisation. EBITDA was INR19.6 crores (11.5% margin) and PAT INR12.3 crores (7.2% margin), hit by a sharp rise in styrene-based raw material prices (about 600 bps of margin impact) and manpower costs (about 200 bps, from a Haryana minimum wage hike). Management said effective price realisation was about 5% in Q1, with a full ~9% price increase expected from Q2 as older-price orders roll off. Growth initiatives include 1.5 million helmets of new capacity, Decathlon, an Italian subsidiary and new products.</overview>

segments.name: Domestic STUDDS (helmets)
segments.commentary: Management cited domestic EBITDA of roughly 16-17% currently, versus about 17-18% in FY26. Q1 price increases were not fully passed through in OEM, CSD/CPC and some export channels.

segments.name: SMK (premium)
segments.commentary: Export EBITDA on SMK was described as about 30-35%. SMK range is INR4,000 to INR15,000 helmets.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 21% of Q1 revenue; target is closer to 30%. Export orders executed in Q1 were contracted before the price rise; new orders are booked at revised prices.

segments.name: Bicycle helmets (Decathlon)
segments.commentary: Bicycle helmet ASPs are about 15-20% below motorcycle helmets. Commercial production expected from October 2026, with Decathlon working like an OEM relationship.

segments.name: Bluetooth and riding jackets (new)
segments.commentary: Management expects INR15-20 crores of revenue from these two categories in FY27. Some products are made in-house and some by contract manufacturers.

segments.name: Italian subsidiary
segments.commentary: Dealer-direct entry planned in Italy, Germany and France. Expected losses of about INR2-3 crores in FY27 and about INR2 crores in FY28; revenue guidance EUR100-125k in FY27 and about EUR1 million in FY28. Management said profits start from year 3, with 10-12% EBITDA margin cited.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 14-15%; normalised 18-20% run rate by Q4 FY27, subject to stable raw material prices.
FY27 revenue growth of mid-teens guided earlier; volume growth now expected at about 10% with 7-8% blended realisation (management said high-teens revenue growth on last call).
Full ~9% price increase (on FY26 base) expected to be reflected from Q2; Q2 realisation expected at 8-9% for OEM/CSD/CPC channels.
Styrene-based raw material cost impact expected to soften to about 300 bps in Q2 from 600 bps in Q1; management expects Q3 and Q4 to improve further.
FY28 standalone guidance: volume growth 13-14% and price realisation 3-4%, implying mid-to-high teens growth (management said this excludes the Italian subsidiary).
At current styrene levels (~INR185 weighted average), PAT margin expected at about 11.5-12%, versus about 13% earlier; management expects a return to FY26 levels by Q4 FY27.
Export mix rising toward 30% could add 200-300 bps to PAT margin, per management's rough estimate.
Total capex of INR76 crores to 30 June 2026 plus INR10 crores of vendor advances; FY27 capex budget INR58 crores (INR7.5 crores spent in Q1); FY28 plan INR31 crores.
